first_impression: Clean-looking nutrition trivia, but it feels too slow and templated for three simple facts.
problems: The hook is not strong enough visually; the first frame is neat but not surprising or thumb-stopping.
Three separate countdowns make the video feel much longer than the payoff deserves.
The same split-screen layout repeats with little variation, so once I understand the format there is no new visual reason to stay.
Some text is small, especially the source and explanatory copy, and may be hard to read on mobile with platform UI.
The banana label appears clipped/mistyped as “BANAN” in one frame.
The round 3 transition has a near-empty frame at 14.0s, which feels like dead air.
The ketchup vs cola comparison may trigger comments about serving size/context because ketchup per 100g is not how most people consume it.
The caption’s RecipeFix plug feels bolted on and makes the post feel like an ad rather than a native food fact post.
fixes: Cut each question to 1 second max before revealing the answer; remove the 3-2-1 countdowns or use a single fast tap-to-reveal animation.
Open with the most surprising fact first, e.g. “Ketchup has more sugar than cola per 100g?” or “Red pepper beats orange for vitamin C.”
Fix the banana text so it never crops; check all safe margins for TikTok/Reels UI.
Vary the reveal layouts slightly between rounds or use food cutouts/photos to make each comparison feel fresh.
Make the key numbers larger and reduce the explanatory paragraph to one short line.
Remove the empty-feeling transition at 14.0s; go directly into the ketchup vs cola slide.
Add a small context note for ketchup: “per 100g, not typical serving.”
Move the RecipeFix promo out of this caption or make the post clearly part of a branded series with a softer CTA.
Shorten the whole video to around 10–12 seconds: three quick questions, three reveals, one summary card.
